title.narrative: CODE – Improved capacities to counter Disinformation in Eastern Partnership. IMS. 2023-2025.

description.narrative: The overall objective of the Project is to improve the resilience of vulnerable population groups in the Eastern Partnerships (EaP) region to obtain fact-based information and enhance critical thinking. The project will contribute to increased capacity of key institutions (media houses, organisations, and governments) to effectively enhance the resilience of vulnerable populations to disinformation. Moreover, the environment (policy and digital infrastructure) will be more enabling for responsible, inclusive and fact-based journalism.

title.narrative: Output 2.1. IMS and targeted partners promote an enabling environment for for responsible, inclusive journalism and fact-based content through alliance building
# of policy papers, draft legislations, revisions and/or amendments to legislation developed by alliances

actual.value: 17 Moldovan and foreign think-tanks, media development institutions and donors have been engaged into promoting legislative changes to ensure balance between freedom of speech, and information security

In Moldova, IMS and our partners built up a solid base for further cooperation between different stakeholders around resilience-building efforts as they developed Moldova Resilience Building Strategic Principles. The synchronizing power of the document is well demonstrated by the fact that more than 20 media stakeholders (including the top TV channels) and 1 state institution have taken it as a guideline for their resilience-building strategies. In Moldova, IMS has provided input to a high-level dialogue between the State and Meta. The input was provided upon request from the CSCCD. IMS input included a written submission for the President Office providing strategic guidance on their messaging to Meta (July 2024). This led to a high-level meeting between the State and Meta in Chisinau in September, which IMS tech expert attended.

actual.value: 5 media partners in Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine have developed driven content strategies based on the insights of the audience segmentation studies.

title.narrative: Output 1.1. Partners utilise the full circle approach and have increased capacity to target vulnerable audiences
Examples of lessons learned by partners when using the full circle approach

actual.value: 34 IMS partners within the ENC have enhanced their audience strategies and content development by utilising audience data generated through CODE. This includes six CODE partners and 28 media and CSO partners in Moldova.

Both Georgian media partners are targeting their interventions on gender, focusing on women communities of Ninotsminda and Akhaltsikhe, and fighting gendered disinformation is Samtskhe-Javakheti. All media partners have a focus outlined on strengthening their work with gendered disinformation.

title.narrative: Output 2.2. Partners promote an enabling tech infrastructure to support their work against disinformation, including solutions on gendered disinformation.
# of selected partners applying additional digital tools for social media monitoring to increase the impact of resilience building

actual.value: IMS has selected a service provider to develop a monitoring mechanism to support our partners in countering disinformation, particularly gendered disinformation. The final negotiations are currently taking place. The mechanism will contribute to monitoring of the 6 digital environment targeting hostile disinformation narratives, which is highly needed to inform IMS partners enabling them to adapt content and counter false narratives.

Seven media partners in Moldova have established a Rapid Response Pilot Group (RRPG) based on a data-driven pre-bunking; this knowledge was cascaded to Georgia and additional media partners in Georgia have launched a RRPG model in September 2024.

title.narrative: Output 1.2 IMS and partners promote data driven resilience building and share experiences with the audience segmentation studies and full circle approach with key institutions to the media sector
# of key institutions reached with awareness about the audience research studies and lessons learned

actual.value: During the reporting period, In Moldova and Ukraine, IMS has provided 69 individual keys to access the audience segmentation studies. 69 individual keys were provided for staff in 37 media, 4 governmental institutions and 12 donor institutions (53 institutions in total).

IMS have influenced national resilience-building efforts in Moldova through ongoing collaboration with the Moldovan Stratcom Centre. This has resulted in the Resilience Building Roadmap, where the audience segmentation data together with available research have informed and led to the suggestion of a strategic framework for multistakeholder cooperation. The Roadmap will be taken as a guideline for the governmental campaigns; in March-April, 18 media partners will design their content ideas to contribute to this collective resilience-building effort. This is also a key example of how CODE successfully enables cooperation between content producers, media houses, CSOs and governmental institutions in resilience-building in Moldova. Another example is, that CODE has bridged key media actors, governmental stratcom bodies, and media monitoring organisations to set up a collective rapid response mechanism called Election Task Force
